_meta.note: The manifest also carries a `sentiment` field. It is NOT a function of `emotion` -- `surprise` splits 48% positive / 52% negative -- so no answer may read it. The label-level `valence` slot below is the function-of-label stand-in, with `surprise` marked mixed. `synonym` is MCQ option text only -- the option list pins the vocabulary, so it never appears as a bare answer. Prose slots carry authored <slot>_why clauses so because() composes a real reason rather than restating the verdict; <slot>_caveat is authored where the generic 'other contexts are possible' reads wrong.

adjective.note: question-side lexical form only; never an answer, or it competes with the label vocabulary

synonym.note: a near-synonym for the label, used ONLY as MCQ option text -- the option list is what pins the vocabulary, so it never appears as a bare answer

activity.note: what the speaker is likely doing, or the interaction under way; answers the guide sheet's Activity family

response.note: bare verb phrase; the template supplies 'I'd ...' or 'Probably best to ...'

tempo.note: pace this emotion lends to speech, music, movement

occasion.note: a setting or occasion you'd expect it at

neutral.expression: an even, unmarked delivery with no strong pitch swings and no edge in the voice
neutral.trigger: ordinary back-and-forth where nothing much is at stake
neutral.activity: getting through ordinary conversation -- passing on a detail, answering a question, or making small talk
neutral.function: a plain hand-off of information, with nothing emotional attached to it
neutral.response: take the line at face value and keep the conversation moving
neutral.occasion: an ordinary day at work or a quiet moment at home
neutral.valence_why: neutral speech carries no strong feeling in either direction
neutral.arousal_why: neutral speech sits at the speaker's resting energy
neutral.expression_why: neutral speech is defined by the absence of any strong marking
neutral.trigger_why: nothing in the delivery suggests the speaker is invested one way or the other
neutral.activity_why: an unmarked delivery is what ordinary, low-stakes talk sounds like
neutral.function_why: neutral delivery adds nothing on top of the words themselves
neutral.response_why: there is nothing in the delivery asking to be handled
neutral.occasion_why: nothing in a neutral delivery marks the moment as a special one
neutral.tempo_why: neutral speech runs at an ordinary conversational pace
neutral.arousal_caveat: speakers differ in how much they let show
neutral.expression_caveat: any one speaker's delivery can depart from the pattern
neutral.trigger_caveat: the audio alone does not show what actually caused it
neutral.activity_caveat: the clip does not show what is really going on around the speaker
neutral.function_caveat: what an emotion is doing depends on who it is aimed at
neutral.response_caveat: the right response depends on who is talking and why
neutral.occasion_caveat: a single line does not pin down the occasion

fear.valence_why: fear is an unpleasant state to be in

fear.activity_why: fear usually means the speaker sees something going badly, or about to
fear.function_why: fear signals a threat and looks for reassurance
fear.response_why: someone who is frightened cannot think straight until they settle
